content: He who fears he will suffer, already suffers because of his fear.
author: Michel de Montaigne
story:
Rather than offering a polite platitude, this observation challenges how we navigate our inner lives. Courage is rarely the thunderous heroics we see in movies; it is the quiet voice at the end of the day that says, 'I will try again tomorrow.' When we wait to feel completely fearless before taking a step, we stay trapped in place.

In Michel de Montaigne's view, genuine strength is not an abstract theory—it is a lived, daily practice. Real strength shows up with a racing pulse and trembling hands. It is the willingness to be vulnerable, to risk looking foolish, and to stand up for what matters even when everything in you wants to hide.
reflectionPrompt: In what area of your life are you overthinking the ideal approach instead of taking the simple, honorable action?
